text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Ekran Bhd's differences with ABB in the Bakun dam project was over the terms relating to cost overruns, Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing told reporters in Langkawi.

-- Forest fires in Indonesia's Sumatra island have been identified as reasons for a perpetual haze over parts of Peninsular Malaysia, particularly Kuala Lumpur, Science Technology and Environment Minister Law Hieng Ding said.
-- Twenty four kilogrammes of heroin originating from Malaysia's southern Johor state was seized in Sydney.
-- Telekom Malaysia Bhd will raise its stake in Thailand's Samart Corp to enable it undertake bigger expansion projects.
-- The United Nations' Declaration on Human Rights needs to be reviewed as it holds a very unsympathetic view of the situation in developing countries, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.
